samples.summary: dispose()'s write revocation is bypassed by an in-flight EditorAPI.paste(): pasteContent() checks readOnly/pasting but not `disposed`, so a clipboard read that resumes after the editor was disposed for a role downgrade still writes to the shared CRDT
samples.evidence: Vector: an anonymous visitor on `/shared/:token` with an *editor* link opens the docs context menu and clicks Paste (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-context-menu.tsx:272` → `void editor.paste()`). `EditorAPI.paste` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3974) awaits `navigator.clipboard.read()` / `readText()` — an await that can span a browser clipboard permission prompt, i.e. arbitrarily long. Meanwhile the share link is re-resolved every 60s (`SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`, packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:88/1115); an `editor` → `viewer` downgrade flips `readOnly`, and the docs-view effect (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:565/590) calls `editor.dispose()` and rebuilds a read-only editor. The captured continuation then resumes and calls `textEditor.pasteContent({html,text})` (editor.ts:3997 / 4005) on the *old* TextEditor, which was constructed with `readOnly === false` (`const textEditor` at editor.ts:2503 is never nulled by dispose). `pasteContent` (text-editor.ts:1659-1667) gates only on `this.readOnly` and `this.pasting`; `this.disposed` — set by TextEditor.dispose at text-editor.ts:6069 — is NOT checked, so the paste falls through `pasteFromParts` → `runPaste` → `applyPastePlan` (text-editor.ts:1544) and writes through the still-writable YorkieDocStore into the shared document. Neutering `api.paste` in `neuterMutations` (editor.ts:1055-1073) cannot stop this: the no-op replaces the member, not the already-running closure. The repo's own precedent shows the required guard: `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` re-checks `this.disposed || this.pasting || this.readOnly` at text-editor.ts:4261 for exactly this reason, and `deferPaste` checks `!this.disposed` at text-editor.ts:1609. Impact is a write past a revoked permission: the docs comment at editor.ts:4497-4501 states the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`, so in a stock deployment this client-side gate *is* the write boundary for a downgraded share token.

samples.summary: After dispose(), getStore()/getDoc() still hand out fully writable handles for a non-read-only editor, so the new disposal-time revocation is name-list-only and bypassable by any stale holder that writes through those accessors
samples.evidence: `dispose()` (editor.ts:4434-4444) sets `disposed = true` and calls `neuterMutations(api)`, and its comment claims "Disposal is the only moment the host can revoke it". But `getStore: () => (readOnly ? readStore : pageSetupGuardedStore)` (editor.ts:3318) and `getDoc: () => doc` (editor.ts:3317-ish) are not touched by disposal, and for an editor built while the session could write, `readStore === docStore` (editor.ts:1123) and `doc = new Doc(readStore)` — i.e. both handles are live and writable after dispose. The pre-existing justification for leaving the accessors out of the allowlist (editor.ts:4503-4509: they are "both backed by `readOnlyDocStore` under `readOnly`, so their mutators are already dead") is true only for the read-only construction path; this delta reuses the same allowlist for a second condition where that premise does not hold. Concretely writable path: `DocsFindBar` builds `new FindReplaceState(editor.getDoc(), () => editor.getStore().snapshot())` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:65-68) and `replaceActive`/`replaceAll` mutate through the captured `Doc` (packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:79-86), which bypasses every neutered `api` member; `packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/bridge.ts:250/330/386` also holds `editor.getDoc()`/`getStore()`. I could not prove a user-reachable interleaving for the find bar (React commits the dispose and the `editor`-keyed effect rebuild in the same flush), hence medium confidence — but any future async holder of `getDoc()`/`getStore()` writes straight past the revocation, and the accessors are the documented escape hatch, so the gate reads as covering more than it does.

samples.summary: MUTATING_METHODS is now a security control for two conditions (read-only mount AND post-disposal revocation) but stays a hand-maintained string allowlist with nothing enforcing that it covers every mutating EditorAPI member
samples.evidence: `MUTATING_METHODS` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1035-1053) is cast through `Record<string, () => void>` in `neuterMutations` (editor.ts:1062), so `tsc` cannot relate the names to the `EditorAPI` interface: a typo or a newly added mutating method silently escapes BOTH the read-only gate (editor.ts:4510) and, as of this delta, the disposal revocation (editor.ts:4444). The only coverage is per-method assertions in packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts (applyStyle, insertLink, insertTable, …) with no exhaustiveness check, and no test at all for the disposal case in the docs package. I verified the list appears complete against today's interface (editor.ts:53-436), so this is a durability/hardening gap rather than a live hole — a mapped type or a test that enumerates the interface would make it self-enforcing. searchedFor is recorded below.

verdict.reason: Verified the whole chain independently. `TextEditor.pasteContent` (text-editor.ts:1659-1668) gates only `readOnly` and `pasting`; it never checks `this.disposed` (set at text-editor.ts:6069), and nothing downstream does either (`pasteFromParts` 1643, `runPaste` 1588 sync path, `applyPastePlan` 1544, `withUndoUnit` 3840 -> `doc.batch`). `EditorAPI.paste` (editor.ts:3974-4007) awaits `navigator.clipboard.read()`/`readText()` — an arbitrarily long await (permission prompt) — and then calls `textEditor.pasteContent(...)` at 3997/4005 on the `const textEditor` captured at editor.ts:2503, which `dispose()` (editor.ts:4434-4454) disposes but never nulls. `neuterMutations` (editor.ts:1061-1067) replaces only the API member, as its own comment at 1056-1059 admits, so the already-running closure is unaffected — and dispose's comment at editor.ts:4435-4442 states disposal is the only moment the host can revoke a stale continuation's write authority, which this path ignores. The downgrade is reachable: shared-document.tsx:88/1115 revalidates the share link every 60s, and docs-view.tsx:578-590 lists `readOnly` in the effect deps so an editor->viewer downgrade calls `editor.dispose()` (565) and rebuilds a read-only editor; the old TextEditor keeps `readOnly === false` baked in at construction (text-editor.ts:717-719, no setter). The write still lands in the shared CRDT because `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:689-693) only unsubscribes and clears `onRemoteChange` while mutators keep writing through the provider-owned Yorkie doc. Trigger is user-reachable at docs-context-menu.tsx:272 (`void editor!.paste()`). The repo's own precedent — `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` re-checking `this.disposed || this.pasting || this.readOnly` at text-editor.ts:4261 and `deferPaste` checking `!this.disposed` at 1609 — shows the guard is expected on resumed writes. Per editor.ts:4497-4501 the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow mode unless enforced, so this client gate is the write boundary. Real, in-lane (write past a revoked permission), and blocking.

verdict.reason: Every factual element of the finding checks out. dispose() (editor.ts:4434-4444) sets `disposed = true` and calls `neuterMutations(api)`, which only overwrites the fixed MUTATING_METHODS name list on `api` (editor.ts:1042-1072); `getDoc`/`getStore` are not in that list and are not otherwise touched by disposal. For a non-read-only editor, `readStore === docStore` (editor.ts:1123) and `doc = new Doc(readStore)` (editor.ts:1124), so `getDoc: () => doc` (editor.ts:3317) hands back a fully writable Doc and `getStore()` returns `pageSetupGuardedStore` (editor.ts:3318, 3290-3310), which forwards all ~30 store mutators and is self-documented as "NOT an access-control boundary" (editor.ts:3251-3255). The comment justifying the accessors' omission from the allowlist (editor.ts:4503-4509) is premised on `readOnly`, which the unconditional disposal-time call at 4444 does not satisfy. I looked for a guard that would make a post-dispose write unreachable and found none: the host cleanup calls editor.dispose() then store.dispose() (docs-view.tsx:565-574), but YorkieDocStore.dispose() (yorkie-doc-store.ts:689-693) only releases the subscription and onRemoteChange — no mutator is disabled, and its own doc comment concedes the store still reads/writes the live Yorkie root. Retained handles exist at docs-find-bar.tsx:65-68 (a Doc captured into FindReplaceState, whose replaceActive/replaceAll write straight through it) and at harness/hunt/bridge.ts:386, docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:496. The DocsFindBar `readOnly` early-return (docs-find-bar.tsx:134) guards only that one UI path, not the revocation itself, so it does not amount to already-guarded. This is an incomplete permission revocation on a role downgrade (viewer downgrade path documented at docs-view.tsx:578-590) — in-lane for authorization/access control and blocking as a clear weakness even though a concrete user-reachable interleaving was not demonstrated.

finding.summary: Async continuations hold a pre-downgrade, fully writable editor/store; the readOnly rebuild does not neuter them, so a write can land after the role dropped to viewer
finding.evidence: `readOnly` is baked into an editor instance at construction — `insertImage` early-returns on the captured `readOnly` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4195) and the API-level neutering happens once at build time (editor.ts:4448-4470). The new deps list rebuilds the editor on downgrade (docs-view.tsx:590) and disposes the old one, but neither `EditorAPI.dispose()` (editor.ts:4400-4413, it only removes listeners/canvas) nor the newly added `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:651-655, which only drops the subscription and `onRemoteChange`) marks the object dead for writes. `insertImageFromFile` awaits `loadFileDimensions` and then the upload, then calls `editor.insertImage(...)` on the editor captured at drop time (image-insert.ts:135-137). Sequence: editor-role visitor drops an image → upload in flight → link downgraded to viewer → effect disposes the writable editor and mounts a read-only one → the upload resolves and the *old* editor writes the image inline into the live Yorkie document, past the permission that was just applied. The same shape exists for any other retained `EditorAPI`/store reference. The diff shows awareness of exactly this pattern (it added `if (this.disposed || this.pasting || this.readOnly) return;` to the clipboard resume, text-editor.ts:4261) but did not extend it to the editor/store handles the host keeps. Fix direction: have `dispose()` neuter the store's mutators (or set a `disposed` flag consulted by `EditorAPI` mutators) so a stale handle cannot write.

verdict.reason: The described vector does not exist in this tree. (1) image-insert.ts guards the post-await resume: `if (editor.isDisposed()) { toast.error(...); return; }` at image-insert.ts:145-148 sits between `await upload(file)` (:144) and `editor.insertImage(...)` (:149), with the same guard on the URL path at :195-198. (2) `EditorAPI.dispose()` does not "only remove listeners/canvas": its first two statements are `disposed = true` and `neuterMutations(api)` (editor.ts:4443-4444), with a comment naming exactly the role-downgrade-mid-upload scenario. (3) `neuterMutations` (editor.ts:1061-1072) overwrites, in place on the same returned object (`const api` at :3315, `return api` at :4514), every entry of `MUTATING_METHODS` (:1042-1052) — which includes `insertImage`, `paste`, `cut`, `insertTable`, `undo`, etc. — so a continuation holding the pre-downgrade handle calls a no-op, not a write. (4) `isDisposed: () => disposed` is exposed at editor.ts:4433 and declared at :408-414. (5) docs-view.tsx:565 calls `editor.dispose()` in the cleanup of the effect keyed on `readOnly` (deps at :590), so the downgrade rebuild does run the neutering. The finding's own recommended fix ("a `disposed` flag consulted by EditorAPI mutators") is the implemented design. `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:689-693) is accurately described as only dropping the subscription and `onRemoteChange`, but stale-handle writes go through the neutered EditorAPI, so no write can land past the applied permission via this path.
